signature_info.description: MS Remote Access serial network driver

attributes.magic: PE32+ executable (native) x86-64, for MS Windows

crowdsourced_ai_results.analysis: The analyzed sample is a legitimate Windows kernel-mode driver, identified as the Microsoft Remote Access Service (RAS) Asynchronous Media Access Control (AsyncMAC) driver (asyncmac.sys). It functions as a WAN miniport driver facilitating network connectivity over asynchronous serial interfaces. The driver performs standard NDIS (Network Driver Interface Specification) operations, including registering a miniport driver via NdisMRegisterMiniportDriver, creating the '\Device\ASYNCMAC' device object, and registering a WAN address family. Concrete behaviors include handling Point-to-Point Protocol (PPP) framing logic (evident in functions like AssemblePPPFrame and AsyncPPPCompletionRoutine which process 0x7e start/stop flags and 0x7d escape characters) and managing serial I/O requests through IoAllocateIrp and IofCallDriver. The driver also reads configuration parameters such as 'MaxFrameSize' and 'IrpStackSize' from the registry. No malicious functionality, persistence mechanisms, or unauthorized data exfiltration behaviors were observed.
